proved: For rightmost r=(X,Y), a j-cap ending b,c extends iff Y<line_bc(X). Thus F3(A;X)<=F4(U;X) ensures a weak Delta A of U extends by r whenever U+r has no five-cap.
It suffices that every terminal pair of a three-cap in A also ends an ambient four-cap in U. Actual blockers necessarily have terminal rank exactly three.
Removing R from A and adding r works iff R hits every blocking triple and does not erase any old polygon's entire selected support.
For |S|<=n+1, every weak Delta of S-r either already works or safely adds r.
At |S|=n+2, deletion-only repair fails exactly when A has three points, T=A+r is a four-cap, and all B+t (B=S minus T, t in T) are convex (n-1)-gons.

A leftmost blue-point insertion lifts this repair obstruction from n to n+1 while preserving five-cap-freeness and absence of the forbidden polygon. The nine-point base therefore supplies sharp repair obstructions for every n>=7.
